title: Reidemeister's theorem for oriented links
statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $D$ and $D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams. Then $D$ and $D'$ represent equivalent oriented links if and only if $D'$ can be obtained from $D$ by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3.
strategy: (<=) is the preceding lemma realizing each move by an ambient isotopy together with transitivity of equivalence. (=>) Let $L$, $L'$ be the represented links and let $H$ be an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy with $H_1(L)=L'$. Choose smooth embeddings inducing $D$, $D'$ (existence of regular projections), restrict $H$ to $L\times I$ to obtain a smooth isotopy of links with the prescribed end projections, apply the general-position item to make it generic without changing the end projections, and apply the singular-times item to convert the family into the required finite sequence of planar isotopies and moves. This is Theorem 3 of Birman-Brendle, Theorem B.1.1 of Ozsvath-Stipsicz-Szabo and Theorem 1 of Queffelec, in the oriented category. The proof consumes the general-position existence item, whose perturbation argument assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ (Sard and parametric transversality), so the countable-choice dependency is declared here.

references.title: Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society (2024); arXiv:2406.18203v1, sections 2-3
Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
